exhibits.title: The Reforged Transformer
exhibits.text:
A great brazier stands at the meeting of two stairs — one climbing from the Attention wing, one climbing from the Diffusion wing — and in its fire the same transformer that reasons over words is reforged to denoise images. Watch the whole rite from start to end, and see that what enters and what leaves are the SAME SHAPE.

1. INPUT. Into the fire go three things: a noisy latent x_t of shape 32x32x4 (a small grid, four channels, already living in the VAE's compressed latent space), a timestep t saying how much noise was added, and a conditioning c — a class, a text embedding, or nothing at all.

2. PATCHIFY. A transformer eats a SEQUENCE, not a grid. So the grid is cut into 2x2 patches on the Patchwork Loom: 16x16 = 256 patches, each of 2x2x4 = 16 numbers, flattened and projected to dimension d. Out come 256 tokens of dim d — an image spoken as a sentence.

3. POSITIONAL EMBEDDINGS. A transformer treats its tokens as an unordered SET; without help, patch (0,0) and patch (15,15) are indistinguishable — the very permutation-invariance the Attention wing cured with RoPE and sinusoids. So each token is stamped with its patch position. Convolution never needed this; a transformer always does.

4. PREP THE CONDITIONING. Timestep and prompt are melted into ONE signal: combined = t_embed + c_embed. Both live in the same d-dimensional space, so their sum is a single vector meaning 'this noise level AND this prompt'. This one vector will steer every block.

5. N DiT BLOCKS. The tokens pass through N identical blocks in the Adaptive Sanctum. Each block is the Attention wing's own skeleton, twice steered by the conditioning: adaLN -> self-attention -> gate -> residual, then adaLN -> MLP -> gate -> residual. Shape never changes: (256, d) in, (256, d) out — which is exactly why the blocks stack cleanly, just as they did for language.

6. FINAL adaLN + LINEAR. One last adaptive norm, then a linear layer projects each token back down to 2x2x4 = 16 values — one predicted-noise patch per token.

7. UNPATCHIFY. The 256 patches are laid back onto the grid, the mirror-image of step 2: patchify compressed grid into tokens, unpatchify expands tokens back into grid. These two are the arms of the machine — like a U-Net's down-and-up arms, but with NO convolution and NO downsampling between them, only attention.

8. OUTPUT. Out of the fire rises epsilon_pred, shape 32x32x4 — the predicted noise, the SAME SHAPE as the latent that went in. The rite has changed the contents utterly and the silhouette not at all.

Stand here and see the symmetry: 32x32x4 in, 32x32x4 out; patchify and unpatchify as folded mirror arms; the transformer block carried whole from the Attention wing and set to a new task. This is not a new machine. It is the old machine, reforged.

exhibits.title: Where the Two Stairs Meet
exhibits.text: This room is a crossing. A stair rises here from the Attention wing and another from the Diffusion wing, and DiT is what stands where they arrive — for DiT is literally attention's transformer dropped, unchanged, into diffusion's framework. Count what was borrowed from the Attention wing: the transformer BLOCK (attention -> residual -> MLP -> residual), carried over whole; SELF-ATTENTION over spatial positions, the exact (n, n) attention derived by hand, now attending patch-to-patch instead of word-to-word; PATCHIFICATION, the very ViT image-tokenization scheme; POSITIONAL EMBEDDINGS, the same permutation-invariance fix as RoPE and sinusoids; even the TIMESTEP EMBEDDING is sinusoidal, the same construction as positional encoding. And what does the Diffusion wing keep? Everything around the network: the forward noising, the reverse sampling loop, classifier-free guidance, the VAE latent space — all UNCHANGED. Only the guts in the middle are swapped. The two wings do not merely neighbor here; they interlock.

exhibits.title: Two Guts, One Task — DiT vs the U-Net
exhibits.text: The old denoiser and the new denoiser do the IDENTICAL job: given a noisy latent, a timestep t, and a conditioning c, predict the noise. They are interchangeable. Swap one for the other and the diffusion framework around them — forward process, reverse process, CFG, latent space — never notices. Only the internal machinery differs. The U-NET is a patchwork: convolution for LOCAL structure, attention bolted on at low resolution for GLOBAL structure, skip connections stitching encoder to decoder, and up/down sampling to march through scales. Its spatial knowledge comes from convolution, which inherently knows where things sit. The DiT throws all of that out: patchify, then plain transformer blocks with attention EVERYWHERE at full token resolution, then unpatchify. No convolution, no skips, no sampling. Its spatial knowledge comes from positional embeddings; its conditioning comes from adaLN-Zero. Same task, same interface, two utterly different sets of guts.

exhibits.title: Why the Field Migrates U-Net to DiT
exhibits.text: Why reforge a denoiser that already worked? Because transformers SCALE more predictably than U-Nets — they obey the same clean scaling laws that carried language models from GPT-2 to the frontier. Pour in more compute and more data and a DiT keeps improving along a smooth, forecastable curve, where a hand-tuned U-Net patchwork sputters. That predictability is why DiT has become the backbone of the newest large generative systems: SORA for video, STABLE DIFFUSION 3 for images, PIXART, and most frontier image and video models built since roughly 2023. The migration runs one way. For small models a U-Net still serves, but for anything large the field has been steadily replacing U-Net with DiT — trading a bespoke architecture for one whose growth it already knows how to buy.

exhibits.title: The Full DiT Pipeline
exhibits.caption: Eight steps from noisy latent to predicted noise. Patchify and unpatchify are mirror arms; the shape 32x32x4 enters and leaves unchanged. The conditioning t_embed + c_embed steers every DiT block.
exhibits.spec:
graph TD
  IN[x_t 32x32x4 plus t plus c] --> PAT[Patchify 2x2 into 256 tokens dim d]
  PAT --> POS[Add positional embeddings]
  POS --> BLK[N x DiT block 256 by d to 256 by d]
  COND[t_embed plus c_embed] -->|steers adaLN| BLK
  BLK --> FIN[Final adaLN plus linear to 16 values per token]
  FIN --> UNP[Unpatchify 256 patches to 32x32x4]
  UNP --> OUT[eps_pred 32x32x4 same shape as input]

exhibits.title: Why the Field Reforged the Denoiser
exhibits.caption: The reason the migration runs one way. Panel (a): as a DiT grows S to B to L to XL, its FID falls along a clean descending frontier (lower is better) — quality follows model compute, with DiT-XL/2 sitting at the frontier's edge, while hand-tuned U-Net baselines (LDM, ADM) sit off that efficient line. Panel (b): pour in training compute and the transformer keeps improving along a smooth, forecastable curve where the U-Net plateaus — the same scaling law that carried language models from GPT-2 to the frontier, now carried into diffusion. The values are stylized and representative; the SHAPE is the lesson. This predictability is why DiT became the backbone of SORA, Stable Diffusion 3, and PixArt.

exhibits.title: Interchangeable Denoisers in One Framework
exhibits.caption: The diffusion framework is identical either way. Only the network in the middle changes: a U-Net of conv, skips, and sampling, or a DiT of patchify, plain transformer, and unpatchify.
exhibits.spec:
graph TD
  FW[Forward noising] --> DEN{Denoiser noisy latent t c to eps}
  DEN --> RV[Reverse sampling plus CFG plus latent space]
  UNET[U-Net conv plus attention plus skips plus up-down sampling] -. swappable .-> DEN
  DITB[DiT patchify plus transformer blocks plus unpatchify] -. swappable .-> DEN
  ATT[Attention wing block self-attention ViT patchify pos-enc] --> DITB
